summary.tldr: Creates an independent commission to review miscarriage of justice applications instead of the Minister of Justice.
what_it_does: Creates the Miscarriage of Justice Review Commission as an independent body with a chief commissioner and other commissioners appointed by the Governor in Council.
Replaces the current ministerial review process, so people apply to the Commission for review of wrongful conviction and related cases instead of to the Minister of Justice.

Gives the Commission power to investigate applications and, if it finds reasonable grounds to think a miscarriage of justice may have happened, direct a new trial or hearing or refer the matter to a court of appeal.
Allows the Commission to provide support to applicants in need, share public information about its mandate, and adopt and publish policies for its work.
Requires annual reports with application, decision and demographic data, and repeals the current regulation on ministerial review applications.
who_it_affects: People seeking miscarriage of justice review
summary.background: The bill replaces Part XXI.1 of the Criminal Code and repeals the Regulations Respecting Applications for Ministerial Review - Miscarriages of Justice. It also makes related changes to several other Acts.
